blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how countries in West Africa collaborate to improve trade and economic growth? This is where economic integration comes in.

blocks.markdown: Economic integration involves the collaboration of different countries to enhance trade and economic cooperation. It aims to reduce barriers to trade and promote economic growth among member countries.

blocks.title: Economic Integration
blocks.text: Economic integration is the process by which countries enter into agreements to reduce or eliminate trade barriers and coordinate monetary and fiscal policies.

blocks.markdown: One of the prominent examples of economic integration in West Africa is the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). ECOWAS aims to promote economic cooperation and integration among its member states.

blocks.title: Understanding ECOWAS
blocks.prompt: What are the main aims of ECOWAS?

steps.text: ECOWAS aims to promote economic cooperation among member states.
It seeks to eliminate trade barriers and establish a common market.
ECOWAS also aims to enhance political stability and peace in the region.

blocks.answer: The main aims of ECOWAS include promoting economic cooperation, eliminating trade barriers, and enhancing political stability.

blocks.markdown: Economic integration can take various forms, such as a free-trade area or a customs union. A free-trade area involves the elimination of tariffs among member countries, while a customs union adds a common external tariff on non-members.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that a free-trade area removes tariffs among members, but a customs union also includes a common external tariff.

blocks.markdown: International organizations like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank play crucial roles in global economic stability. The IMF provides financial assistance and advice to member countries, while the World Bank focuses on long-term economic development and poverty reduction.

points: ECOWAS aims to promote economic cooperation and stability in West Africa.
A free-trade area eliminates tariffs among members, while a customs union includes a common external tariff.
The IMF provides financial assistance, and the World Bank focuses on economic development.
